topics.title: Persian period study: The Persian Empire, 559-465 BC

outcomes.text: Describe Cyrus' background and accession, and his conquests of Lydia and Babylon.
Explain Cyrus' attitude towards conquered peoples, including his liberation of the Jews.
Describe the construction of Pasargadae and the circumstances of Cyrus' death.

subtopics.title: Cambyses II and the accession of Darius, 530-522 BC

outcomes.text: Describe Cambyses' conquest of Egypt and his attitude towards the Egyptians and their culture.
Explain the circumstances of Cambyses' death and Darius' overthrow of Smerdis/Bardiya/Gaumata.
Explain Darius' pacification of the empire, including restoring control over Babylon.
Describe the construction of Susa, Persepolis and the Egyptian canal.
Describe Persian expansion into the Aegean, the campaign in India and the war with the Scythians.
Explain Persian culture and religion under Darius, and his organisation and administration of the empire.
Explain the causes, course and consequences of the Ionian Revolt, and Persian relations with Athens before it.
Describe Mardonius' expedition of 493-492 BC and the expedition to Greece in 490 BC and its aftermath.

subtopics.title: Xerxes I and the Greeks, 486-465 BC

outcomes.text: Describe the death of Darius, the accession of Xerxes and the suppression of revolts in Babylonia and Egypt.
Describe the invasion of Greece: preparation, the journey, Thermopylae, the sack of Athens and Salamis.
Explain Persian military organisation and fighting techniques.
Describe the completion of Darius' building projects, the Battle of Eurymedon and Plutarch's 'famous peace'.

topics.title: Greek depth study: From Tyranny to Democracy, 546-483 BC

outcomes.text: Explain the concept of tyranny and the actions and characteristics of the Peisistratids' rule.
Describe the political structure under the tyrants.
Explain Harmodios and Aristogeiton's part in Hipparchus' assassination and the change in Hippias' tyranny afterwards.
Describe the Spartan invasion to remove Hippias and the fall of Hippias.
Describe the accession of Polycrates and his treatment of political opponents.
Explain his policy towards Egypt and Persia and Spartan and Corinthian opposition.
Describe the building and engineering achievements of Polycrates.
Explain Maeandrius' failed succession, his offer of democracy and its withdrawal.
Explain Persian interference in Samian politics and support for Syloson, and compare with Athenian tyranny.

subtopics.title: The emergence of democracy in Athens

outcomes.text: Explain Cleisthenes' rivalry with Isagoras, Spartan involvement and the introduction of isegoria.
Explain Cleisthenes' reforms: tribes, demes, phratries and the reorganised boule.
Explain the Spartan attempt to restore Hippias and Corinthian arguments against restoring tyranny, including Cypselus and Periander.
Explain Athenian democratic policy toward Persia, the ten strategoi, and support for and withdrawal from the Ionian revolt.
Explain the development of democracy in Ionia after the revolt.
Explain Themistocles' navy and the Battle of Marathon and their significance for democracy.
Explain changes to the archonship and the onset and uses of ostracism.
Explain the roles and treatment of Miltiades, Themistocles and Aristides in the new democracy.
Study the prescribed ancient sources for the tyranny to democracy depth study.

topics.title: Greek depth study: Athens in the Age of Pericles, 462-429 BC

outcomes.text: Explain citizenship after the reforms of Ephialtes and Pericles, and Pericles as a leader.
Explain the workings of the ecclesia, boule, archontes and strategoi, and the assembly's role in law making.
Explain the role of public speaking and Sophist tuition, and the ostracism of Cimon and Thucydides.

subtopics.title: Athens, Sparta and Pericles' foreign policy

outcomes.text: Explain rising tensions with Sparta: refused help against the helot revolt, the Long Walls and Athens' growing power.
Explain Athens' leadership after the Persian Wars: the Delian League, the Athenian Empire and moving the treasury to Athens.
Explain the Megarian decree, and Pericles' strategy in the Archidamian War and its impact, including the plague.
Explain the importance of Pericles' building programme and the Acropolis buildings' cultural and religious significance.
Explain criticisms of the programme, including tribute money and the trial of Pheidias.
Describe the Panathenaia and City Dionysia and the significance of Athena and Poseidon.
Explain Athenian views of themselves in the Funeral Oration.
Describe the role and position of women in daily life, including marriage.
Explain women's position in the democratic system and the status of citizen women after Pericles' citizenship law.
Explain what Medea, the Arrephoroi and Aspasia show of Athenian attitudes to women.
Study the prescribed ancient sources for the Athens in the Age of Pericles depth study.

topics.title: Greek depth study: Alexander the Great, 356-323 BC

outcomes.text: Describe Alexander's youth, Olympias' influence and his relationship with Philip.
Explain Alexander's character and beliefs, including adopting Persian dress and customs.
Describe his relationships with Parmenio, Cleitus, Callisthenes, Hephaestion and Antipater.
Explain the initial reasons for the expedition against Persia.
Describe the battles at the Granicus, Gaugamela and the Persian Gates.
Describe the pursuit of Darius and Bessus, the Indus Valley campaign and the mutiny at the Hyphasis.
Explain the difficulties on the return journey to Babylon.
Explain his changing aims and views of Persians, and the nature and role of his foundation cities.
Explain the murder of Philip and differing interpretations.
Explain the burning of Persepolis, the murder of Cleitus and the mass marriages at Susa.
Explain Alexander's death and the differing explanations.
Explain the use of cavalry, the phalanx and specialist troops, and the army's weapons and armour.
Explain the significance of tactics at the main battles.
Explain siege warfare at Tyre and the Aornus Rock, and Alexander's relationship with his army.
Study the prescribed ancient sources for the Alexander the Great depth study.

topics.title: Longer period study: The foundations of Rome, 753-440 BC

outcomes.text: Explain the Aeneas and Romulus foundation myths and Romulus' political initiatives.
Explain Rome's relationship with the Sabines, the role of the Senate and Romulus' death.
Explain Numa's succession, diplomacy and religious policies, and Romulus' religious initiatives.
Describe Romulus' organisation of the army and conflicts with neighbours, and Tullus Hostilius' conflict with Alba Longa.
Explain the legal system under Tullus Hostilius and Ancus Marcius' expansion of Rome.
Assess the nature and origin of the historical evidence, including archaeological and geographical issues.
Explain how each monarch gained power and the methods used to secure it.
Explain Servius Tullius' reforms and the tyranny of Tarquinus Superbus.
Explain the development of the city, omens ascribed to Servius Tullius and the Tarquins' wealth.
Explain the army's reorganisation, the significance of victories and Tarquinus Superbus' military record.
Assess the literary and archaeological evidence for the period.
Describe the removal of Tarquinus Superbus and the creation of the early Republic, the Consulship and the Senate.
Explain the impact of the Republic on plebeians and patricians and their growing tensions.
Describe military challenges: the Battle of Silvia Arsia, Lars Porsena's invasion and the Battle of Lake Regillus.
Assess the nature and origin of the evidence for the period.
Explain the development of plebeian influence: Sicinius, the First Secession and the Volero Publilius uprising.
Explain the Decemvirates, the Second Secession, the Twelve Tables and the Valerio-Horatian laws.
Explain change and continuity in patrician and plebeian lives, and the impact of Appius Claudius' family.
Explain the military implications of the plebeian revolts and the impact of war on Roman politics.
Assess the nature and origin of the evidence for the period.

topics.title: Roman depth study: Hannibal and the Second Punic War, 218-201 BC

subtopics.title: Reasons for the outbreak of the war

outcomes.text: Explain the impact of the First Punic War and the Treaty of Lutatius on Rome and Carthage.
Explain the significance of Hamilcar and Hasdrubal's colonisation of Iberia and the Carthaginian war party.
Explain Hannibal's motivations, including Hamilcar's influence and the threat of Roman expansion in Iberia.
Explain Hannibal's leadership at Saguntum, the Rhone and the Alps crossing.
Explain his tactics in Italy at Trebia, Trasimene and Cannae.
Explain his failures: marching on Rome, countering Fabian tactics, making peace, keeping allies and supply routes.
Explain the leadership of Sempronius, Flaminius, Servilius, Varro and Paullus and Roman mistakes.
Explain Fabius Maximus' impact: dictatorship, religion for confidence, and Minucius' failure.
Explain Scipio Africanus' appointment, Iberian campaign, Senate debate with Fabius and invasion of Africa.
Explain why Hannibal left Italy: Carthaginian pressure and supply problems.
Explain the Numidian cavalry's support for Rome and unrest caused by the invasion of Africa.
Describe the Battle of Zama and the reasons for and consequences of Hannibal's defeat.
Study the prescribed ancient sources for the Hannibal depth study.

topics.title: Roman depth study: Cleopatra: Rome and Egypt, 69-30 BC

outcomes.text: Describe Cleopatra's family, Macedonian heritage and likely education.
Explain her character as depicted in the sources: charm, humour and courage.
Describe Ptolemy XII's death, Cleopatra's first years and the civil war with Ptolemy XIII.
Explain her relationship with her brothers and Arsinoe and the expansion of Egyptian territory.
Explain her relationship with her subjects, her Graeco-Egyptian image and the promotion of Isis.
Explain Rome's relationship with client states and the importance of Egypt for Rome.
Describe Cleopatra's meeting with Caesar, their relationship, the birth of Caesarion and her visit to Rome.
Describe Mark Antony's position after Caesar's death and the meeting at Tarsus.
Explain the Antony-Cleopatra relationship's significance and the Donations of Alexandria in the breakdown with Octavian.
Explain the causes of the war between Octavian and Antony and Cleopatra, and the preparations.
Describe key events of the battle, the roles of Octavian, Agrippa, Antony and Cleopatra and the reasons for the outcome.
Compare views of the battle in the sources and its impact on Cleopatra and Antony.
Explain the suicides of Cleopatra and Antony and their significance for Octavian.
Study the prescribed ancient sources for the Cleopatra depth study.

topics.title: Roman depth study: Britannia: from conquest to province, AD 43-c.84

outcomes.text: Explain the reasons for invasion: Caesar's attempts, southern British politics, and Claudius' position in Rome and Caligula's preparations.
Describe the invasion: preparations, crossing the Channel, and the Medway and Thames encounters.
Explain Claudius' role and the invasion's propaganda value, and the second phase with Vespasian and the Fosse Way.
Explain Ostorius Scapula's campaigns and Didius Gallus' policies towards the Silures and Brigantes.
Explain the significance of the appointments of Veranius, Suetonius Paulinus, Petronius Turpilianus and Trebellius Maximus.
Describe the campaigns of Bolanus, Cerialis and Frontinus and the reasons for their policies.
Explain Agricola's campaigns and achievements, and the influence of different emperors.

subtopics.title: Cooperation and the effects of Roman rule

outcomes.text: Describe the tribes' submission to Claudius at Camulodunum and the creation of client states.
Explain Romanisation: urbanisation, cultural, religious and lifestyle changes.
Explain the economic impact of the army and traders, and early developments at Camulodunum, Fishbourne and Aquae Sulis.
Explain the resistance campaigns of Caratacus, Boudicca, Venutius and Calgacus and their success.
Explain the Roman response and the sources' portrayal of resisting Britons.
Study the prescribed ancient sources for the Britannia depth study.
